Job Description

Position overview:

SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory is seeking a research associate in the Linac Coherent Light Source (LCLS) to develop new approaches to low-dose imaging that exploit correlations between photons. The successful candidate will have a leading role in a Laboratory Directed Research and Development (LDRD) project spanning simulation, instrument development and experimental demonstration. The candidate will build Monte Carlo models of imaging systems, design and commission a prototype in a SLAC laboratory, and compare measured images with simulation to quantify the achievable reduction in dose. The project brings together scientists across LCLS, SSRL and SLAC's detector groups with external university partners, and is closely linked to a DOE X-ray quantum imaging program. The candidate is expected to have core interests in quantum or correlated imaging, physics simulations and experimental setup.

The candidate will be required to engage in and drive scientific research on low-dose correlated imaging, from simulation through to experimental demonstration. The dissemination of scientific outcomes through peer reviewed publications, as well as presentations at meetings/conferences, is expected. SLAC is committed to fostering a work environment that promotes inclusion, diversity, equity and accountability. We encourage all qualified applicants to apply; you do not need to meet all the Preferred Qualifications to be considered.

Note: The Research Associate role is a fixed term staff position. Appointment duration is for 2- year fixed term
, with the possibility of extension. Assignment duration is contingent upon project needs and funding.

Applicants must provide evidence of either a recently completed PhD degree or confirmation of completion of the PhD degree requirements prior to starting the position. Applicants should also include a cover letter, a curriculum vitae which includes a list of publications, and names of three references for future letters of recommendation with the application.

Your Specific Responsibilities Include

Develop and demonstrate low-dose correlated imaging by:

Building and running Monte Carlo radiation-transport simulations to optimize the imaging geometry, materials and detectors, and to establish the limits of the method
Designing, assembling and commissioning a prototype imaging system, including mechanics, detectors and data-acquisition electronics
Developing data-acquisition and analysis software, and comparing results with conventional imaging
Planning and performing imaging experiments on test samples, and quantifying image quality as a function of dose
Extending the method toward advanced detector technologies and multimodal imaging with collaborators
Collaborating with other scientists, postdocs, students, engineers, and technical staff to execute experiments and perform forefront research
Disseminating research results through peer reviewed publications and presentations at scientific meetings and conferences

To Be Successful In This Position You Will Bring

Ph.D. in Physics, Applied Physics, Medical Physics, Nuclear Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field, and course work or research experience in the following:
Radiation detection instrumentation and fast timing electronics, and a demonstrated ability to develop, design, and optimize scientific instrumentation.
Monte Carlo radiation-transport modelling (e.g. FLUKA, Geant4 or MCNP) and scientific programming (e.g. Python) for data analysis.
Familiarity with quantum imaging, imaging statistics, or medical imaging is an advantage.
Demonstrated record of scientific productivity through publications.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to work and communicate effectively with a diverse population.
Demonstrated ability to work in a team environment.

Day-to-day work is primarily animal husbandry: rearing and feeding larvae, maintaining the phytoplankton cultures used as larval food, caring for adult sea urchin and sea star broodstock, and keeping the rack systems clean and running. Because the rearing and housing methods were developed by

collaborating labs and are new to Hopkins, the technician will play a key role in adapting and troubleshooting them. The role also includes microinjecting eggs with transgenic constructs, keeping meticulous records of animals, cultures, and transgenic lines, and providing occasional administrative support to the lab. Experience with aquatic animal husbandry, such as rearing marine invertebrate larvae or maintaining seawater or recirculating aquarium systems.

Histological procedures involving fixation of tissue and staining specimens with stains that do not require microscopic control in proceeding from step to step.

Because the rearing and housing methods were developed by

collaborating labs and are new to Hopkins, the technician will play a key role in adapting and troubleshooting them. Histological procedures involving fixation of tissue and staining specimens with stains that do not require microscopic control in proceeding from step to step.
Maintenance and transfer of established cell lines where the culture conditions are well defined.

Job Description Summary:

GW’s Department of Microbiology, Immunology, and Tropical Medicine ( MITM ) conducts innovative, fundamental, basic and translational research for HIV / AIDS and neglected tropical diseases. MITM is searching for a full-time Laboratory Technician, MITM for Dr. Maggirwar’s laboratory. Dr. Maggirwar’s laboratory focuses on the vascular complications associated with HIV -1 infection. Our goal is to use the immune cells isolated from the blood samples derived from laboratory animals and HIV -infected/non-infected control individuals to study the role of platelets in modulating immune response in HIV -1 pathogenesis in context to viral persistence, cardiovascular disorders and cerebral small vessel diseases.

This position will be responsible for performing experiments in a biomedical research laboratory and contributing to general maintenance of the laboratory, equipment and supplies. Provides general maintenance of the laboratory. Maintains Good Laboratory Practice, complies with biosafety guidelines, keeps inspection records, and generates SOPs and reports.

About This Opportunity

At Freenome, we are seeking a Senior Research Associate to help grow the Process Development team within Genomics Early Development. The ideal candidate will work to optimize next-generation sequencing (NGS) processes and develop new methodologies on our multiomics platform. This person will work cross-functionally with Research & Development, Automation, Computation Science, Quality, Regulatory, Laboratory Operations, and Program Management on the development, characterization, scale-up and transfer of complex methodologies, processes and assays to Operations. You are passionate about contributing to developing life-saving diagnostics through early cancer detection, and you will have a significant impact on the continued growth of an organization dedicated to changing the entire landscape of cancer.

The role reports to the Senior Manager of Genomics Early Development. This role will be an onsite role based in our Brisbane, California headquarters.

What You’ll Do

Apply hands-on knowledge of molecular biology, nucleic-acid biochemistry and next generation sequencing to develop and optimize NGS based methods and processes following principles of Design Controls for IVD development.
Design and execute experiments to characterize and optimize NGS workflows, converting prototypes into high-throughput automated assays.
Performs analysis and data visualizations to answer experimental questions and identify areas for workflow optimization.
Present findings at team meetings and prepare technical reports for internal and external stakeholders.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate process improvements into the overall diagnostic workflow.
Participate in generating Standard Operating Procedures and Work Instructions with Laboratory Operations and Clinical Laboratory for transfer.
Troubleshoots complex workflow issues, design and execute root-cause determinant experiments, and propose effective data-driven solutions.
Maintain detailed records of experiments, data, results and methodologies in compliance with Good Laboratory and Documentation Practices (cGLP, cGDP).

Must Haves

Bachelor’s in Molecular Biology, Genetics, Biochemistry, or a related field with a minimum of 4 years of experience.
Strong molecular biology background and hands-on experience in NGS based techniques, including nucleic acid extraction, library preparation, and sequencing.
Hands-on experience with plasma handling and cfDNA in NGS workflows and with low-volume, plate-based assay formats on automated liquid handlers.
A proven track record of planning and executing complex experiments.
Strong written and verbal communication skills. Effectively communicates with team and cross-functional partners.
High attention to detail - record and document accurate, objective observations, assess impact, and perform troubleshooting as needed.
Excellent problem-solving skills, proactively looks for potential roadblocks, characterizes root causes to problems and collaborates with appropriate stakeholders.
Ability to work independently as well as part of a cross-functional team.
Flexible and adaptable to change and embrace a fluid work environment.

Experience in molecular diagnostic assay development in an FDA regulated environment for an in vitro diagnostic (IVD) under design control is desirable. Lab Developed Test (LDT) /CLIA and CE-IVD experience will also be considered.
